why: I compared each check's PASS/FAIL conditions with its expect line. Check 1 asserts padding with a given fill and with the default space, and that padLeft is exported as padLeft(s, width, fill). The expect line itself writes that signature, so the parameter-order check comes from its words. Check 2 only tests inputs that are equal in length or longer and come back unchanged. Check 3 requires a Markdown heading for each exported function and real section content under it, which is what "has a section for every function" asks. Check 4 requires exit 0 and no failing tests, which is what "npm test passes" means. The stricter items are tests in test/strutil.test.js and README sections in export order. Both sit under "Advisory (does not affect PASS/FAIL)". No PASS/FAIL condition has a mutation test, a branch or file-scope rule, or an exact-wording rule.
